content.question: Which search strategy does Eclat use, and when is it generally faster?
options: Breadth-first search; faster on very sparse datasets with long TID lists.
Random search; faster when the minimum support threshold is very low.
Depth-first search; generally faster when the dataset is dense and the TID lists are manageable.
Best-first search with a hash-tree; faster on high-dimensional numeric data.
content.answer: Depth-first search; generally faster when the dataset is dense and the TID lists are manageable.
